diuided into

THE ARGVMENTOF GENESIS.
maner, facob otherwrſe called Iſrael, with al his progenie, deſcended from
the Land of Canaan into Ægypt, and were there entertayned. So this booke
contayneth the hiſtorie of two thouſand three hundred & odde yeares. And
it may be diuided into eight partes. The firſt contayne th the Creation
Feauen and Earth, & other Creatures, and laſtly of Man chap. 1. &2.
The ſecond part is vf the trangreſſion e fal of man, & his caſting out
Paradiſe, of multiplication o men, and of ſinne, though ſtil ſeme Were
iuſt, of the general floud, that drowned al except eight perſons, & fewy other
liuing creatures of the earth. from the third chap. to the 8. The third part is
of the new increaſe, & multiplication of the ſame. from the 8. chap. to the
11. The fourth, of the confuſion of tongues, & the diuiſion o nations. in
the it. chap. The fift relateth Abrahams going forth of his countrie, Gods
promiſe, that in his ſeede al Wations should be bleſſed, & the commandment
Circumciſion, from the 12. chap. to the 21. The ſix th part recounteth the
progenie, and other blegings, eſpecially the great vertues of Abraham, Iſaac,
and Iayob. from the 21. chap. to the 37. The ſeuenth part reporteth the ſel-
ling oy Iofeph into Ægypt, and his aduancement there. from the 37. chap. to
the 46. The eight and laſt yart is of Iacob, and his progenies going into
Æyypt, their intertainment there, and of lacobs, and finally of Ioſephs
death. in the fiue laſt cahpters.
The ſignification of the markes herevſed, for
direction of the reader.
The numbers in the argumentes of chapters point to the verſe, where the mat-
ter mentioned beg inneth.
This forme of croſſe † † I in the text, sheweth the beginning of euerie verſe.
T he numbers in the inner margent ouer againſt the croſſe:, shew the number
of verſes in the ſame chapter.
This marke ſig nifieth that there foloweth an Annotation after the chapter,
vpon the word, or wordes, wherto it is adioyned. The number alſo of the
ſame verſe is prefixed to the Annotation.
The ſe foure prickes :: shew that there is an Annotation in the margent, vpon
that place. And when manie occurre, the firſt anſwereth to the firſt marcke,
the ſecond to the ſecond, and ſo forth. In like maner the citations of places
in the inner margent, are applied to the authores alleaged.
But when there be more ſuch marginal annotations, then may eaſely be ap-
plied, we vſe the letters of the Alphabete for direction.
This forme of a ſtarre I * I in the text or annotations, pointeth to the explica-
tion of ſome word or wordes, in the margent.
Sometimes we put the Concordance of other Scriptures in the inner mar-
gent of the text.
VVe haue alſo noted in the margent, when the Bookes of holie Scripture (or
partes thereof) are read in the Churches Seruice. For their ſakes, that defire
to read the ſame, in order of the Eccleſiaſtical Office.
